brief: A hurrying figure crossing a moonlit clearing, murmuring to himself as he goes, a paper-fan spirit pointing at him from the roots; the Vetāla and Dādī watching; Śuka perched on a stump.

The rose-mist pusher spirit with its dozen hands: one tilting a small boy's head towards a book, one lifting a spoon to a sleepy ghost's lips, one setting a foot on a path; the Vetāla pointing at each; Dādī laughing.

A small round spirit of warm rose-coloured mist with a dozen tiny hands, like a starfish, bustling in: one hand pushing a book towards you, one a spoon, one setting a foot on a path; the Vetāla seated on a root beginning a tale with a raised finger; Dādī and Śuka watching.
A quiet image of a small clay lamp whose flame stays steady while a cracked clay body beside it falls apart; ink-and-watercolour in the style of old Indian manuscripts, soft ivory paper.
The twelfth tiny hand of the rose-mist spirit holding out a small clay cup, empty and very still; Śuka tilting his head; Dādī nodding; the Vetāla watching with half-closed eyes.

A burning-ground grove at night: a pale, almost see-through spirit walking backwards out of the dark, its edges fading like old ink, a trail of fading footprints behind it; the Vetāla hanging from the śiṃśapā tree yawning; Dādī and Śuka watching.

The Vetāla seated on a tree root, folded like a long grey umbrella, eyes closed, telling a tale; Dādī and Śuka sitting before him; the faint backwards-walking spirit crouched beside; at the dark edge of the trees Lubdhaka leaning in to listen, the lantern low.
An old king in a forest looking up at a tree where a corpse hangs and a lamp-lit face seems to speak; ink-and-watercolour illustration in the style of old Indian manuscripts, soft ivory paper.
